stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML technologies including transformers, safetensors, and text-generation.
The mention of Llama-3 indicates continued industry focus on large language models from Meta.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: ChatGPT to face tougher regulation in the EU
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: ChatGPT is now classified as a Very Large Online Search Engine under the EU's Digital Services Act (DSA).
OpenAI will face increased regulatory scrutiny in the EU regarding its platform.
Key areas of concern for regulators include risks to minors, user mental health, and illegal content dissemination.

stories.title: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules
stories.author: Barbara Moens, Financial Times
bullet_points: Major AI platforms like ChatGPT and Reddit are subject to stringent new online safety regulations in the EU.
The news highlights the growing regulatory pressure accompanying the rapid expansion of large-scale AI and online platforms.
This signals a significant industry shift toward increased compliance burdens for tech giants operating in the European market.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama serves a large developer base, currently reaching 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents entirely on local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated support for Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved by leveraging MLX, Apple's native machine learning framework.
This integration is currently available in a preview build, signaling optimization for the Apple ecosystem.

stories.title: InstructMesh: Selective Refinement of Generative 3D Models for Fabrication
stories.author: Stefanie Mueller
bullet_points: InstructMesh addresses a critical flaw in current generative 3D models: prioritizing visual plausibility over geometric accuracy for fabrication.
It is an interactive post-generation refinement tool allowing users to selectively repair generated 3D models.
Key functionalities include targeted operations like sealing voids or adjusting local thickness based on user region selection.

stories.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
stories.author: Oliver Lemon
bullet_points: Investigates how Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) errors in user input can compromise the safety of Embodied AI (EAI) models.
Findings demonstrate that ASR errors can cause EAI models to accept and execute harmful instructions, directly reducing overall system safety.
The research uses simulations combined with benchmarks (SafeAgentBench, POEX) to analyze how different types of ASR errors impact semantic structure and safety.

stories.title: REPLICANT: Learning Policies for Evading and Hardening Malware Detectors
stories.author: Fabio Pierazzi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Replicant,' a deep reinforcement learning framework designed to test malware detector robustness.
Addresses a critical gap in current research by modeling realistic adversaries who do not have privileged access to detector internals.
Focuses on the practical task of malware evasion and hardening detection systems against sophisticated attacks.

stories.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
stories.author: Oliver Lemon
bullet_points: Investigates how Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) errors in user input can compromise the safety of Embodied AI (EAI) models.
Findings demonstrate that ASR errors can cause EAI models to accept and execute harmful instructions, directly reducing system safety.
The research uses simulations combined with benchmarks (SafeAgentBench, POEX) to analyze how different types of ASR errors impact AI safety.

stories.title: Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root
stories.author: 0xcc.io via ucirello
bullet_points: The vulnerability, named Omarchy, allows any user process to escalate privileges to root.
This represents a critical security flaw with high potential impact on affected systems.
The news originates from a security research blog (Lobsters), indicating a serious vulnerability disclosure.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across diverse hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Car owners want tech they can ignore
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Consumers are growing weary of the excessive and often buggy technology being integrated into modern vehicles.
The latest JD Power survey indicates that the most valued automotive features are often those that are subtle and require minimal user attention.
This suggests a potential market shift away from feature bloat towards more intuitive, less intrusive in-car experiences.

stories.title: Phil Schiller is leaving his biggest jobs at Apple
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller is stepping down from his leadership roles at Apple.
His departing roles include heading the App Store and Apple events.
Schiller will retain his Apple Fellow title and continue working on unspecified initiatives.

stories.title: Debian won’t ban AI code from its Linux distribution
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Debian has updated its policy to permit the use of AI tools by developers contributing to the Linux distribution.
The decision acknowledges that responsible AI usage can boost developer productivity within the project.
The policy asserts that generative AI is subject to existing standards and is not exempt from them.

stories.title: Instagram cracks down on AI accounts pretending to be human
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: Instagram is increasing its crackdown on deceptive AI accounts masquerading as human influencers.
The platform is renaming its 'AI creator' label to 'AI-generated profile' for greater transparency.
This move addresses user dissatisfaction regarding the prevalence of hard-to-detect fake AI personas on the site.

stories.title: NASA's next "great observatory" begins mission to widen our view of the Universe
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: NASA is launching a new, large-scale astronomical observatory mission.
The survey data generated is incredibly vast, requiring massive display capabilities (e.g., half a million 4K TVs).
The project aims to significantly expand humanity's observational view of the Universe.

stories.title: Pocket's AI made my game ideas real. Now Meta controls the results.
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Pocket's AI tool facilitates the creation of interactive mobile 'gizmos' for game ideas.
A key limitation is the difficulty in sharing these creations outside of Meta's platform.
The story highlights the growing influence of major platforms (like Meta) over emerging creative technologies.

stories.title: A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A massive 12TB data leak from Steam has exposed a significant amount of unreleased or lost PC gaming content.
The leak reportedly contains cut content from established titles like Portal 2.
It also includes tantalizing hints and potential assets related to unreleased content, such as Half-Life 2: Episode 3.

stories.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
stories.author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Meta is actively piloting the use of robotics within its data center infrastructure.
The robots are being tested on tasks currently performed by human technicians.
This signals a trend toward increased automation in large-scale tech operations.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: Privacy requests sent to 100 companies resulted in significant operational friction.
Many companies exhibited confusion or failed to properly handle data deletion requests.
The study highlights systemic issues in how large organizations manage user data privacy.

stories.title: Learning a Size-Weight Frontier for Synthetic-Augmented Inference
stories.author: Kaizheng Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the bias risk when using synthetic data to augment scarce real-world datasets for statistical inference.
Introduces a general framework for synthetic-augmented inference applicable across multiple related tasks.
The core contribution is a 'size-weight frontier' that quantifies the optimal balance between synthetic sample size and its assigned weight.

stories.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
stories.author: Ruoran Xu
bullet_points: The field of neural-network optimization is evolving beyond simple Adam variants.
Optimization design space is expanding to include matrices, layers, and time-dependent policies.
Modern optimization must account for practical constraints like sharding and low-precision computation.

stories.title: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification Guarantees for Neural Operators
stories.author: Nicolas Boullé
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of Neural Operators: the lack of inherent uncertainty quantification in their predictions.
Introduces a 'split conformal framework' to provide rigorous, probabilistic guarantees around the neural operator's output.
The method ensures that a specified confidence band contains the true solution with high probability, which is crucial for reliable AI deployment.

stories.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
stories.author: Ruoran Xu
bullet_points: The field of neural-network optimization is moving beyond simple Adam variants.
The design space for optimizers is expanding to include matrices, layers, and temporal policies.
Modern optimization must account for practical constraints like sharding and low-precision computation.

stories.title: DARTS: Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery for Model Merging
stories.author: Seganrasan Subramanian
bullet_points: The paper introduces DARTS, a method for tuning representations during model merging of LLMs.
Model merging often causes 'representation bias' (drift in hidden states) when combining fine-tuned LLMs.
DARTS specifically addresses this bias in decoder-based models, an area less explored than encoder-based models.

stories.title: A Formal Limitation on Learning Human Language From Textual Corpora
stories.author: Ryan Cotterell
bullet_points: The paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of language understanding, questioning if meaning can be recovered solely from utterance form.
It derives upper bounds on the probability that a decoder can recover intended meaning from a textual representation, including LLM hidden states.
The research models language use as a joint distribution across meanings, contexts, and utterances.

stories.title: Phoneme- and Word-Level Metrics Using Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Forced Alignment Evaluation
stories.author: Gerhard Jäger
bullet_points: Introduces two novel, reference-free metrics (PCMI and WACS) for evaluating forced alignment.
These metrics leverage self-supervised (SSL) speech representations to bypass the need for manual timestamp annotations.
Aims to enable large-scale and multilingual analysis in speech processing tasks.

stories.title: Ladders in Chaos: When, How, (and Perhaps Why) Does Test-Time Scaling Improve LLM Machine Translation
stories.author: Vlad Niculae
bullet_points: The paper investigates two test-time scaling methods (sequential and parallel) for improving LLM machine translation.
Sequential sampling was found to have a higher performance ceiling and generate a more diverse sample pool, especially with limited sampling budgets.
The research contributes to understanding the practical application and comparative effectiveness of different LLM inference strategies in translation tasks.

stories.title: NL2AGBench: Benchmarking LLM Auto-Formalization for AlphaGeometry
stories.author: Ziliang Zong
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap in LLMs' ability to translate informal math problems into formal representations.
The work introduces NL2AGBench to benchmark LLM auto-formalization specifically for systems like AlphaGeometry.
This research is crucial for advancing neuro-symbolic AI systems that require domain-specific language (DSL) inputs for theorem proving.

stories.title: Blind Men and the Elephant: Probing the Epistemic Myopia of LLMs under Long-Tail Divergent Knowledge
stories.author: Xing Sun
bullet_points: Introduces ElephantBench, a new closed-book knowledge probe designed to test LLM capabilities.
Addresses the limitation of standard QA by probing whether LLMs retain divergent or non-canonical accounts of long-tail facts.
Uses an auditable, graph-based pipeline to generate questions based on naturally occurring disagreements in low-exposure web corpora.

stories.title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
stories.author: Xing Sun
bullet_points: ContextPilot addresses the challenge of managing growing working contexts in long-horizon LLM agent tasks.
The research proposes using fine-grained Reinforcement Learning (RL) for proactive context management.
It aims to overcome limitations in existing methods, which are restricted to basic context editing tools like search, deletion, and summarization.

stories.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents
stories.author: Nan Li
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current AI evaluation: testing a model's ability to maintain state and make sequential decisions in interactive dialogue games.
The study uses a 2B open-weight model in the LM Playschool Challenge, identifying that failures often stem from local decision errors rather than just broad knowledge gaps.
The paper proposes a 'diagnosis-guided post-training recipe' to improve small-model performance in complex, stateful interactive environments.

stories.title: Sliding-window beats linear attention
stories.author: Emy Gervais
bullet_points: Quadratic attention in LLMs leads to unsustainable memory and energy consumption as token count increases.
The core problem is the indefinite storage requirement for keys and values in standard attention mechanisms.
Sliding-window approaches are being investigated as a viable alternative to linear attention to mitigate quadratic scaling issues.

stories.title: Automate Flutter's New Split Package Migration with AI Agent Skills
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article discusses automating the migration of Flutter projects to standalone UI packages (material_ui and cupertino_ui).
It leverages 'dart-sdk-skills' to empower an AI coding agent for this migration task.
This represents a practical application of AI agents in streamlining complex, framework-specific development workflows.
